problem: Overlapping ngrams counted as independent rarity evidence, below-threshold dense similarity still raised the fused score, and source-lane diversity could repeatedly spend the small result budget on the same query cue.
changes: Count the strongest rarity match per connected query-overlap group; repeated copies of a cue count once. Exact query coverage remains available.
Keep raw dense similarity in audit fields, but only a qualified dense channel contributes to the fused score. Apply the integer accessibility offset after rounding.

Keep the highest fused result, then prefer remaining candidates that cover independent unrepresented query cues; use type/source/subject diversity and score for ties. Eligibility and both byte limits remain enforced.
